newsitem.title: USA: Dow slammed in biggest point loss since mid-July.
newsitem.headline: Dow slammed in biggest point loss since mid-July.

text.p: A huge late afternoon sell program sent the Dow industrials skidding 80 points to its biggest point loss since the July stocks sell-off as investors raced to lock in profits after a spectacular November.

"A wave of sell programs hit the market. Big stocks were punished and small caps performed somewhat better. It appears there was profit-taking after a superb month of market action in November," said Alan Ackerman, a market strategist at Fahnestock and Co.
The Dow industrials shed 1.21 percent to about 6443.
It was the blue chip index's biggest point drop since July 15's 161.05-point slump amid heightened earnings jitters.
The Dow soared about 500 points or eight percent in November and many were awaiting a pullback.
Birinyi Associates Inc said the late sell program wiped 50.31 points off the Dow. In total, Birinyi tracked three buy and three sell programs Tuesday that erased 69.72 Dow points.

The broader market also ended well off its highs, although the tech-studded Nasdaq Composite clung to minor gains that helped it set its seventh consecutive record closing high. The index rose one to about 1300.37, its first finish above 1300.
Winners beat losers 12-11 on very heavy NYSE volume of about 516 million shares.

As for the last 10 minutes of frantic trading that took the Dow from down 50 points to down 80, Douglas Myers of Interstate Johnson/Lane said, "This is an old fashioned sell program that took it down. ... This is the type of blowoff the market needs to take a little wind out of the sails. Give it a chance to rebalance, reallocate and wax philosophic."
Bellwether IBM, which hit a fresh nine-year high of 166 intraday, slipped 1/8 to 163-1/8 -- its first lower close in about two weeks.
Among other Dow components, GE lost four to 99-1/4, Procter & Gamble shed 3-7/8 to 104-3/4 and United Technologies was off 3-1/2 to 136-1/2.
The long bond rose 1/32 to yield 6.36 percent.

Treasury prices hit the day's highs after news that seasonally adjusted new single-family homes sales fell 8.7 percent in October, a much sharper decline than economists had forecast. But Treasuries turned lower later as heavy corporate issuance weighed on the market, including $850 million of IBM 100-year debentures.

Interest-rate sensitive stocks came under more selling pressure after enjoying recent strong gains. Wells Fargo lost 4-1/4 to 279-1/2, Freddie Mac shed three to 111-5/8 and BankAmerica was off three to 98-3/4.
Among individual shares, Hutchinson Technology soared 19-1/2 to 72-1/4 after forecasting first-quarter ended December 29 earnings would far exceed analysts' expectations.
Silicon Graphics surged 3-3/8 to 23-5/8. Goldman Sachs upgraded the stock to its recommended list from market performer.
U.S. Robotics tumbled 7-1/8 to 73-3/4.
Needham & Co cautioned that the modem maker may be facing a weak quarter as it makes the transition to new technology, market sources said. Needham declined comment.
Summit Technology added 2-3/8 to 8-3/4. Summit said the FDA approved its plan to expand farsightedness clinical trials using the SVS Apex Plus excimer laser system.
Centocor surged 5-3/8 to 34-3/8. Morgan Stanley raised its price target and Salomon reiterated its strong buy.
Market Facts surged 8-1/4 to 42-3/4. The provider of custom market research cited an increased awareness of the stock among investors and additional market makers.
The Nasdaq Composite rose 0.55 to 1300.37, a record.
The S&P 500 fell 8.28 to 748.28.
(Figures official as of 1645 EST/2145 GMT).
-- Wall Street Desk 212-859-1721
